subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-chat isolation be solved by extending sender-scoped session/thread bindings, by adding automatic per-user group subagents, or by proving the orchestration as a Feishu plugin experiment first?
rationale: The current code has partial primitives but the requested automatic per-user subagent lifecycle changes product behavior and security boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design the narrow Feishu isolation seam first
options.body: Use current sender-scoped session and subagent binding primitives as the base, define the missing memory/config/lifecycle boundaries, and only then implement the approved seam.

options.title: Prototype in the Feishu plugin
options.body: Allow a plugin-scoped experiment to validate routing, cleanup, quotas, and admin controls before expanding SDK or core contracts.

options.title: Defer heavy group subagent orchestration
options.body: Close or pause automatic group subagents for now while keeping narrower session-routing and threading issues open.

recommendation.title: Design the narrow Feishu isolation seam first
recommendation.body: Use current sender-scoped session and subagent binding primitives as the base, define the missing memory/config/lifecycle boundaries, and only then implement the approved seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged implementation area is Feishu ACP/subagent session binding, which is the likely base for any maintainer-approved design.
